body:
Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (0) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. Lost start records trigger another lead ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: 7d566f0

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>Start is now tried only once per stall, in the run that posted the stall's first LEAD-SILENT alarm
>(before the fire), via try_start/start_after_alarm. Failed or uncertain starts are no longer retried
>("no retry"), so a lost LEAD-STARTED post cannot cause a second fire on the next watchdog run.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>start_after_alarm() uses a trusted LEAD-STARTED comment as its only durable evidence that the
>watchdog has fired the lead task. If the trigger succeeds but post_quietly() cannot publish that
>comment, start_lead() returns success and the next watchdog run can fire the task again for the
>same stall.
>
>

2. No automatic restart when a handover's successor dies ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: 4a78b56

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>The diff changes the spec (docs/design/m6d-watchdog.md) rule 2 so that the one-start check counts
>only architect/watchdog LEAD-STARTEDs, excludes a lead's own handover start, and adds a LEAD
>ONLINE-after-alarm check. It also documents the handover-successor-dead path as getting one start
>and adds tests in B-5 for handover cases. The room.py code is not shown changing in this diff, so
>the fix is a spec-side resolution of the same contradiction: the code now is to match the documented
>intent, and the documented intent now explicitly includes the start after a handover whose successor
>never joined or died. This resolves the finding per the "change the docs" option applied to the
>spec, but the CHANGELOG/ARCHITECT text is not part of this diff.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>start_after_alarm treats any trusted LEAD-STARTED newer than since as the stall's one start
>(rule 2). On the ordinary path since is the last progress time, and cmd_handoff writes the step
>before the outgoing lead runs start-lead, so the successor's LEAD-STARTED is always newer than
>that progress. The result is that a successor whose start didn't take, or that joined and died
>before its first step change or push, gets alarms and reminders but never the watchdog start. The
>spec's per-path list ("released after a handover whose successor never came: one takeover or plain
>start") and the CHANGELOG and ARCHITECT text all promise that start.
>
>
3. Unrecorded rooms receive owner reminders ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: 4a78b56

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>The design doc now states that the owner reminder applies only when room N is recorded as the
>current room in PLAYBOOK.md or the machine block, and adds a test for "No reminder when no room is
>recorded." This addresses the finding at the design level by requiring a recorded current room
>before reminders; the code change itself (requiring current_room() to equal a.room) is not in this
>diff, so the fix is documented rather than implemented here.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>waiting_request() rejects a different current room but permits current_room() to return None.
>If the state says waiting for owner without a valid room in either the playbook or machine block,
>an old request in the watchdog's room can produce a reminder despite no record that this is the
>current room.
>
>
4. Other alarms delay owner reminders ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: 4a78b56

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>Updated the watchdog design doc so the owner-waiting reminder counts only its own reminders for that
>request (not intervening state-unreadable alarms), scoped state-unreadable alarms to the newest run
>after the stall's last other alarm, and added a test case for an intervening state-unreadable alarm
>not delaying the reminder.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>cmd_watchdog() passes the waiting request's timestamp to stall_alarm() without restricting it to
>alarms about that request. If state was unreadable after the request and its alarm was posted before
>state recovered, the unreadable alarm counts as the waiting reminder and postpones the first
>reminder until its own 12-hour interval expires.
>
>
View medium (2)
5. A renewed state outage misses its alarm ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: 4a78b56

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>The design doc was updated so that only the newest run of state-unreadable alarms (those after the
>stall's last other alarm) counts toward the stall; an outage that recurs after an ordinary alarm
>gets a fresh first alarm. Also added a test expectation for a new first alarm for an outage that
>comes back after an ordinary alarm.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>unreadable_state_alarm() now passes a predicate that keeps every earlier state-unreadable alarm
>since progress, even across an intervening ordinary alarm. If state recovers, an ordinary stall
>alarm is posted, and state becomes unreadable again without newer progress, stall_alarm() treats
>the previous outage's alarm and retry count as belonging to the new outage.
>
>
6. Overlapping runs can start two leads ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: d5a5286

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>The watchdog now starts a lead only in the single run that posted the stall's first alarm (try_start
>/ posted_first from stall_alarm, lines 90-93 and 311-319 of the diff). stall_alarm returns True only
>for the run that posted the first alarm, and a later or overlapping run gets posted_first=False and
>can only print a note. Rule 2 also checks for trusted LEAD-STARTED newer than SINCE, and start_lead
>gained --seen/--replacing guards (room_moved_on, lease_moved). This narrows the window so two runs
>don't both try, though it is not a true atomic lock; the fix is a different design from the
>suggested durable claim, but it addresses the overlapping-start race.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>start_after_alarm() checks for an existing start and then calls start_lead() without atomically
>claiming the stall. If two watchdog runs overlap, both can pass that check and start_refusal()'s
>separate comment check before either posts LEAD-STARTED, allowing both to fire the task.
>
>

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
